# Runbook for Online Training Jobs

**Audience:** feed_recommendation_retrieval_modeling oncall. 


**Goal:** Safely maintain & restart online-training (OT) jobs without tripping scribe admission controls or accidentally training from scratch.


*Distilled from the June 2026 SEV0 recovery (*[*S669133*](https://www.internalfb.com/sev/669133)*, *[*S675860*](https://www.internalfb.com/sev/675860)*).*



---

## Ensure OT jobs have robust configuration

**1. Register your model in TMS.** A model must be registered (and not expired) for any of the flows below to work.


[dropdown: &#60418;]mvai online-training-mgr register-and-run -m <MODEL_ID> --reason "<why>"

[dropdown: 2. Make sure your training_launch_service config (in configerator) can restart training gracefully. By default a restart does not auto-resume from the latest checkpoint [a][b][c]— pin the resume arg in source/aiplatform/training_launch_service/models/<MODEL_ID>.cconf:]

**2. Make sure your training_launch_service config (in configerator) can restart training gracefully.** By default a restart does **not** auto-resume from the latest checkpoint — pin the resume arg in source/aiplatform/training_launch_service/models/<MODEL_ID>.cconf:


- --snapshot -1 for OS/U2I and i2i
- --checkpoint-version -1 for ESR

*[6/17] NOTE: We (*Evan WelchPaul Lu*) are creating diffs to the launcher entrypoints to make this “-1th checkpoint” behavior standard. Currently adding it for all cases will fail when training from scratch. *


Check the model's launcher for the exact flag (it varies by domain). The durable launcher fix that makes "resume-from-latest-if-available, else cold-start" the default is [D108680504](https://www.internalfb.com/diff/D108680504). Verify a restart actually resumed via the [global_step Scuba](https://fburl.com/scuba/mvai_metrics/jf1qwftv) — qps/global/* global_step should be large and incrementing (near-zero = trained from scratch).

![[image — use --describe-images for description]](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdnbnUeF9G01KfngOwqb4rADFSkGUifsk15Mmhg325qEirwRr-oG91DdzhglkpvXhv6KZ5KGDmXvzT85xVqInOMp80YvOcIzUyo5Wl_py29ZCxSUMtjDXqBHhZLDjk2o1UCGv-Btpkdceg7OonjcsIQ8YYUSy-nHlrch2zq9yHzxp0c=s2048?key=XyQqMyKdk5eFC5lfLJ9vdw)

**3. Preserve your app layer** so it can't be auto-deleted out from under a long-running job (convert-fire-app → archive + preserve the fbpkg, then pin that version in the TMS config):


[dropdown: ]mvai convert-fire-app

fbpkg archive  <app_pkg>:<version>     # exempt from auto_delete_oldest

fbpkg preserve <app_pkg>:<version>     # ephemeral -> permanent


[dropdown: Why expiry is set?]

4. **Clear any expiry / TTL from TMS.**


*Why expiry is set?*

Depending on how the OT job was started and if the app-layer was ephemeral, MVAI online-training-mgr may have set an expiry (see S675448) in the TMS config corresponding to the ephemeral app layers expiration date at the time of job creation. 


Why it matters?

This expiry / TTL can kill your OT job even if you’ve followed steps 1-3 above.


*How to clear the Expiry / TTL?*

There are 2 cases: 

1. OT jobs that are RUNNING (with upcoming expiry) and whose training_launch_service config has a properly preserved app-layer (steps 1-3 above)

[dropdown: tms-cli start-training-job <MODEL_ID> --reason "..."]**tms-cli update-training-job <MODEL_ID> --expiration_type NEVER_EXPIRE --env production --reason "..."**

[dropdown: ]

1. and those that have already been EXPIRED (due to TTL).

[dropdown: How to confirm expiry is removed?]**tms-cli unexpire-training-job <MODEL_ID> --expiration_type NEVER_EXPIRE --env production --reason "..."**

**tms-cli start-training-job <MODEL_ID> --reason "..."**


[dropdown: # or]


*How to confirm expiry is removed?*


[dropdown: ]** ****tms-cli get-tms-config <MODEL_ID>     # TTL Expiration Type: NEVER_EXPIRE**

**# or**

** mvai online-training-mgr print -m <MODEL_ID>   # Expires On: NO EXPIRY SET**


[dropdown: ]** Healthy = Intended State: ONLINE_READY · MAST: RUNNING · Expires On: NO EXPIRY SET.**

## How to update OT jobs

### [Most updates] Stateless changes

A stateless update may be patching the app-layer, an entitlement or hardware change, or any other fire-arg / app-arg edit that does **not** invalidate checkpoints):


1. **Edit and land the change to TMS config.** Keep TMS state online_ready — do **not** pause / set OFF (that forfeits the in-place-restart exemption and re-gates you on admission control).

The command above help you create TMS config diff to update commonly changed fields

[dropdown: &#60418;]# remove --override and --hardware flag if you are certain don't need them

# use --help to check all supported fields

# use --dry-run for sanity check without create diff

ifr-os-tools ot-config-diff diff -m <MODEL_ID_1> -m <MODEL_ID_2> --app <APP-LAYER> --nodes "5x8" --override "--locality-constraints region,gtn" --hardware GRANDTETON

[dropdown: ]


1. **Kill the running MAST job** (via UI or CLI). Wait for TMS to auto-launch a new MAST job verison.

[dropdown: &#60418;]meta ai.mast-job kill --job-name=mvai-training-online-<MODEL_ID> --confirm --reason="<why>"

[dropdown: ]

1. **Confirm the new version reflects your change** — e.g. kill v4, wait for v5 to start, check the **Definitions** tab (or CLI):

[dropdown: ]meta ai.mast-job describe --name=mvai-training-online-<MODEL_ID>

[dropdown: Docs: Revert & Ban Tooling wiki &middot; MLHub R&B UI]


4. (Remediation for OT status/expiry) Check app-layer status and expiry status after launch and periodically 

You can use the cli tool below to quickly check multiple model app-layer and expiry status

[dropdown:   --revert-to-time-iso "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS-07:00" --ban-checkpoints --message "<why>"]ifr-os-tools ot-config-diff show -m <MODEL_ID_3> -m <MODEL_ID_2> -m <MODEL_ID_3>

[dropdown: tms-cli update-revert-ban-plans --revert-ban-plan-ids <PLAN_ID> --update-to-state READY]![[image — use --describe-images for description]](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfZt7c96zscMldYcPSGrKaApYsqWPuC3FekOQuDaiw7ftwS4OJ1FLuVPiK49Rg6mYMkJyIwOW_ejtCuIjqH_gWtjoUGFCBQz6J6U3NBkGdJM8p4RLs5uWJdiDLU8bsnCud6lfW15zGR-FJBcA9t4z_FmkaM13SEjPi1JCXpBF1K5z8uFhQ=s2048?key=XyQqMyKdk5eFC5lfLJ9vdw)



### [Revert & Ban Checkpoints or Snapshots] Resume from a previous state

To ban contaminated checkpoints/snapshots and resume from a last-known-good point, use the TMS **revert & ban** tooling. Its block plan keeps the models online_ready while it stops the job, reverts, and bans — so the resume is a continuation, not a gated new start.


Docs: [Revert & Ban Tooling wiki](https://www.internalfb.com/wiki/DAI_Managed_Training_Service/Componentized_Online_Training_Service/Training_Management_System/Revert_and_Ban_Tooling/) · [MLHub R&B UI](https://fburl.com/mlhub/7q2bqcex)


[dropdown: But always check the specific app-layer and model launcher entrypoint for the correct value.]feature install --persist tms_cli

tms-cli create-revert-ban-plan --external-tracking-id <SEV> --model-ids <id1,id2,...> \

  --revert-to-time-iso "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS-07:00" --ban-checkpoints --message "<why>"

tms-cli update-revert-ban-plans --revert-ban-plan-ids <PLAN_ID> --update-to-state READY

tms-cli get-revert-ban-plans --revert-ban-plan-ids <PLAN_ID>     # monitor (~5–10 min)

[dropdown: Always manually clear the checkpoint metadata cache after revert and ban. Each model has a Manifold metadata file (info.json) that can hardcode the next expected checkpoint — example: manifold://mvai_traincache/tree/online_training/<MODEL_ID>/info.json (confirm the exact path/bucket for your model). TMS tooling does not reliably clear it, so after a revert-and-ban — or any time a model won't resume from the current checkpoint — clear it manually:]

You may find it convenient to configure via the CLI but monitor in the UI (e.g. [here](https://www.internalfb.com/mlhub/models/model_series?filters=%7B%22key%22%3A%22AND%22%2C%22children%22%3A[%7B%22key%22%3A%22EQUALS_ANY_OF_EXACT_TEXTS%22%2C%22field%22%3A%22MLHUB_TRAINED_MODELS_ALACORN_EXTERNAL_TRACKING_ID%22%2C%22value%22%3A[%22675448%22]%7D]%7D&activeTab=SEV%20Mitigation&subTab=ALL_MODELS)):

![[image — use --describe-images for description]](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcbSIELOy1Lxcz-qYCy0vCxb8OyL-GleJQzRt4WxBhQBhSCudFYrNH6JeoZjZQiwKj_F_Hij3Ckvv_EqZsxGm3kilbev5HWAoXwCDhTJ28PBc3o-VQ7TR6puHFlZlzo1JiZMKzbK_RjM330YwPKsO3MwLDOccsw1HxEE3W2dSOKY-YXpeU5ZA=s2048?key=XyQqMyKdk5eFC5lfLJ9vdw)


**Be aware of the scribe catch-up window first.** Online jobs read scribe data starting some number of seconds in the past — the **catch-up seconds** set in the train/config provider. Before reverting, look up that value: if you genuinely believe the data is corrupted, a plain restart will just re-read the bad window. Use the **TMS CLI / wiki flow (not the UI)** to keep your jobs **blocked** until enough time has passed that the catch-up window no longer overlaps the corrupted period, then resume.

- U2I Lookback: [code pointer](https://www.internalfb.com/code/fbsource/[d1e7989cacc4f2b37e9007f131f088accdae46e1]/fbcode/minimal_viable_ai/sandbox/umia_hstu/ifr_umia_v1_u2i/mtml_roo/trainer_config_providers.py?lines=128)
- I2I Lookback: [code pointer](https://www.internalfb.com/code/fbsource/[27f288d4d34d806b0c118164e99878fe3bc3ab8f]/fbcode/minimal_viable_ai/sandbox/umia_hstu/ifr_i2i/ifr_i2i_mc3_dev/trainer_config_providers.py?lines=74)

But always check the specific app-layer and model launcher entrypoint for the correct value.


[Experimental]: If you cannot wait for the scribe catchup window to pass and want to resume OT sooner, consider adding DPP-settings to enable “Scribe-tailing” D108448929



**Always manually clear the checkpoint metadata cache after revert and ban.** Each model has a Manifold metadata file (info.json) that can **hardcode the next expected checkpoint** — example: manifold://mvai_traincache/tree/online_training/<MODEL_ID>/info.json *(confirm the exact path/bucket for your model)*. TMS tooling does **not** reliably clear it, so after a revert-and-ban — or any time a model won't resume from the current checkpoint — clear it manually:


[dropdown: ]mvai online-training-mgr -m <MODEL_ID> -c

[dropdown: ]The impact of not clearing will be that the previous checkpoint is marked invalid, however the new version of the MAST job will repeatedly try to read that version and fail. If you notice this symptom, first try clearing the cache.

### [Bypassing admission control] Restarting an expired / paused critical job

The OT scribe quota (ONLINE_TRAINING_SCRIBE_USAGE) is enforced at the **Feed umbrella tenant** (root/Facebook/Feed), which runs chronically over quota ([S669133](https://www.internalfb.com/sev/669133)) — check current usage on the [scribe Scuba](https://fburl.com/scuba/mast_supporting_service_resource_usage_info/6lm3u2pp). Admission control gates **new TMS starts**; an online_ready job restarted in place bypasses it ([Admission Control WP post](https://fb.workplace.com/groups/710550224249570/permalink/1213594903945097/)).


In the rare case an important, long-running OT job (launch backtest / holdout) has **EXPIRED** or gone **PAUSED**, naively bringing it back to **ONLINE_READY **will be treated as a new start and subject to admission control, but you can try this to be sure:


[dropdown: ]mvai online-training-mgr unexpire-training-job -m <MODEL_ID> --reason "<why>"   # may be rejected by admission control

[dropdown: This should be put in the front page (I also found UI shows wrong information about online status, it show &ldquo;ONLINE&rdquo; but won&rsquo;t restart or maybe the restart checkpoint interval is long)]

If the job is critical and the tenant is overquota, please reach out to the **managed_training_service** oncall (OT support: [group](https://fb.workplace.com/groups/280672176819805)) to troubleshoot a bypass. Be prepared to show the model had been running for a long time and was stopped by accident (i.e. that it’s not a net new job)

## Ongoing Improvements to Online Training


- **Default to graceful resume in the launcher.** Make --snapshot -1 / resume-from-last-checkpoint the **default** behavior in our launcher code, while still supporting an explicit train-from-scratch path. Today configs that omit the arg silently cold-start (root cause behind [S675860](https://www.internalfb.com/sev/675860); partial fix in [D108680504](https://www.internalfb.com/diff/D108680504)).
- **Deprecate the ****info.json**** checkpoint-metadata file.** This cached file hardcodes the next expected checkpoint and has caused many resume-from-scratch errors. We're considering **removing it entirely**. Relatedly, the TMS tooling is **flaky about whether it clears this metadata** during revert-and-ban — near-term we'll make that clearing more reliable so the manual -c step isn't required.
  - [ ] T276144655: ensure cache invalidation is made more robust
  - [ ] 
- **Enable runbook to enable scribe tailing to skip bad data.** There is DPP-level tooling to **activate tailing scribe** — forcing OT jobs passing particular filters (e.g. model type) to strictly tail the scribe logs and skip past the corrupted data window. This gets models training again sooner without waiting for scribe_catchup_seconds to pass. Example diff from SEV0: D108448929
  - [ ] Confirm w/ DPP this is a general lever they want customers using vs reaching out to oncall
